purpose: Choose HUD widget priority, changed digits, cursor advance, cached values and timer-bar cells, with an ordered native write/service journal over the existing canonical HUD/world state.

inputs: All raw word score/cache/icon/fare/cursor/position/player-count/timer/divisor/fade/bar values and every value of the original byte fields. HudValues imports bytes zero-extended and borrows existing canonical state; it owns no duplicate world or image.
Live numeric digit buffers and arbitrary current/previous byte pairs, includingFF; live closed decimal divisors and failures remain a service. Cursor/index additions wrap at16 bits.
Live four-byte single/cumulative mask tables, arbitrary values, full TimerBarPointer binding, inherited plane/latch/GC state.
outputs: Ordered exact-width cache/shared-world writes and number/sprite/bar requests; each consumed prefix is published before the synchronous service. The declared next stage, normal complete consumption and matching working projection are checked.
Glyph sprite204+raw AL; two border requests; per-byte scanner draw/skip and sentinel completion. Bar mask family/index, partial cell/color, wrapping preceding-cell count and three-row positions.
effects: Glyphs use the accepted primitive boundary; decimal conversion uses the already closed entries and preserves numeric leading zeros/live divisor semantics.

Timer bar has no screen read. The platform programs sequencer index2 and the selected live table byte, writes rows0/96/192 in order, forces maskF, then on growth writes preceding complete cells right-to-left. It preserves inherited GC/latch/write/read controls and full pointer segment. Do not add a destination read or force a write mode.
Normal finish rejects remaining effects, wrong next stage, pending bar or projection mismatch. An abnormal child status returns the consumed prefix immediately; no future planned stores are applied.
preconditions: Ordinary disjoint code/data, stack, image and immutable resource descriptors. Services are synchronous; they do not mutate HUD/world inputs or caches except the owned digit cursor through the called HUD scanner. The bridge imports that child cursor on return before checking projection.

Original byte members are zero-extended in the typed view. No restriction on raw word signs, cache initialization, delays or histories. All cursor/bar positions wrap; no clipping or saturation beyond the original score cap.
Bar cursor is initialized by hud_bar for a changed width; next is called for remaining full cells. Individual scalar successor properties additionally cover every raw word, including zero wrap.

native: closed decimal conversion through its existing entries
services: Live mask selection and ordered three-row pixel transactions

targets: Original named near calls and DrawHudBorders tail to DrawTransparentSprite
indirect.classification: Shared changed_digits retains the RedrawChangedFourDigitNumber+27 return word even for the two/six-digit wrappers. No invented callback, session role or digit limit.

owned: HUD caches/cursor/bar width and operations on the existing score cap, negative timer and fade fields. HudValues is an ephemeral working projection, not a second persistent owner.

Current numeric buffers remain with closed decimal conversion. This unit reads the current and prior buffers at matching wrapping index; no buffer rewriting, leading-zero trimming or cached-value recomputation.
borrowed: Lives, multiplier, journey count, both players carried/icon/destination/fare values, PlayerCount and layout cursor positions. Other native units keep their existing writes/ownership.
Page histories and sprite/image resources remain with rendering; the bar pointer and masks are backend resources.

cache_writers.statement: Normal196-word clear at D:2648..27CF includes bar/cache/cursor HUD words. Incoming DF and live far workspace pointer remain original. Cached icon words at2800/2802 are outside that span and are explicitly assignedFFFF by LoadCurrentLevelState.

memory.projection: After each journal store, compare all imported fields at the matching cut. Before a child, publish the consumed prefix and bind all native service operands. After a successful child, import its cursor only, then compare every field. The following stage reimports canonical state; future effects are never published ahead of their cut.

assumptions: B normalizes37 ordinary canonical words/zero-extended byte members and the ordinary disjoint stack at the branch cuts; all raw scalar boundaries remain symbolic. Full RAM and device/ABI behavior are independently C.

Eight refresh-stage properties, arbitrary-prefix append, typed field/byte frames and dependence compose the native effect boundary. Actual bridge import/store/service/finish/returned kernels are separately checked; normalized memset/memcmp are explicit byte loops, not an opaque library assumption.

Raw pixel transactions, complete machine ABI/flags, page/resource bindings, aliases outside ordinary disjoint resources and full session composition are C/D. No unrestricted formal VGA or session claim. Closed decimal behavior discharges its existing child contract.
eliminated: Native code contains no machine register model, addresses, segments, memory accessors, ports, dispatch or stack frames.

Priority, digit comparison, cursor advancement, cache selection and timer-bar arithmetic come from ordinary native functions. The bridge consumes their actual values and rejects private-only mutations.
retained: Lives may update before score. Score caps unsigned DX:AX at999999, writes caches before number service and jumps directly to timer when changed. Otherwise journeys precede first-player icons; each icon change draws icon and destination then skips fare/multiplier. Second-player handling requires exact PlayerCount==2.

Fare chooses player one first, then player two only in two-player mode; clear-pending can force zero. Clear flag is reset after the optional number service. Multiplier follows fare. CursorX is set to fare X even when there is no fare redraw.

Changed scanner stops only on currentFF, not oldFF. Unchanged digits still advance cursor6. Arbitrary numeric byte values map to glyph204+AL; no ASCII conversion, digit clamp or zero suppression. Scanner index wraps and a missing sentinel retains the original unbounded scan; no budget added.

Negative raw timer storesFFFF. Signed nonnegative fade step becomesFFFE and fade level adds−2 with wrap. Nonnegative timer divides unsigned by the live divisor; divisor0 retains unsupported status and the original pushed DS frame.

Quotient/cache comparison is signed. Shrink clears only one partial three-row cell and leaves other old cells. Growth decrements width before mask/index selection, including0 toFFFF; group-span subtraction wraps. Partial writes precede the full-mask descending fill. All rows use wrapping96-cell offsets and live inherited latches without a read.

evidence.method: Eight native refresh stages cover every original HUD W/WB and immediate service in order; next-stage equality checks preserve every early jump and scheduling priority. Actual-C output properties record an arbitrary published journal position and all branch continuations. Independent input-byte frame/dependence profiles, arbitrary-prefix append and projection-field/frame properties close the typed working state. Glyph/border/cursor/scanner and partial/full bar-cell cuts cover the remaining decisions. Native bar family/index uses arbitrary live table bytes as service replies; physical transactions and complete ABI/flags/stack/session composition remain C/D. Closed decimal entry behavior is a borrowed contract, not re-encoded here.

amiga.finding: HUD purpose does not prove DOS digit ordering, word arithmetic, cache scheduling, latch/mask behavior or pixels. DOS remains the oracle; no Amiga equality is claimed.

negative_results.reachability: 25/25 final-comparison controls intentionally fail only at their specified assertion. See reachability.json.
negative_results.diagnostics: Initial kernel preprocessing lacked stdlib and a modeled memset body; corrected with explicit scoped normalization. Unused cut labels are suppressed only in compiled harnesses. No final timeout or memory cap is credited as proof.
